steps.text: Gather all ingredient, and preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

Make sauce: Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook and stir ground beef in the hot skillet until browned and crumbly, 5 to 7 minutes. Add onion and mushrooms; sauté until onions are transparent. Stir in pasta sauce and cook until heated through. Set aside.
Make filling: Combine cottage cheese, ricotta, eggs, and Parmesan in a medium bowl and set aside.

Spread a thin layer of meat sauce in the bottom of a 13x9-inch dish. Layer with uncooked lasagna noodles, cheese filling, mozzarella, and meat sauce. Continue layering until all components are used, reserving 1/2 cup mozzarella. Cover the dish with aluminum foil.

Bake in the preheated oven for 45 minutes. Remove foil and top with reserved 1/2 cup mozzarella. Continue baking until cheese is melted, about 15 more minutes. Let lasagna stand for 10 to 15 minutes before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Easy Lasagna with Uncooked Noodles
raw_recipe.description: This lasagna with uncooked noodles uses mushroom, onion, and ground beef in jarred pasta sauce layered with cottage cheese, ricotta, and mozzarella.

review.reviewBody: I have always made my lasagne without cooking the noodles first. **I do not buy the no-cook noodles, I use the regular ones and it always turns out great!*** The important thing is to make sure all the noodles are covered with sauce. You can actually add quite a bit of water to the sauce to make sure everything is covered & it still turns out great. I have sometimes just added water to the baking pan after layering to ensure everything is covered - have never been disappointed with the results. - ALSO - this is not something you can make ahead & bake later as the noodles will turn to mush if they sit in the liquid too long before cooking.

I used 48 ounces of sauce. Then added about half of another jar I had in the fridge. Then I added about 1 jar water. I seasoned the sauce with garlic/ onion powder and Italian seasoning. I also added a can of fire roasted tomatoes diced. I had a bunch of random needed to use cheeses. So I used Monterey jack, mexican blend, mozzarella and sharp cheddar. My daughter is really picky so I didn't use any meat or the canned mushrooms. She also won't eat it if there's any ricotta/ cottage cheese mixture in it. (I've tried.) I used a box of lasagna noodles plus a box with a few leftover sheets in it. I used a lasagna deep dish aluminum pan for easy clean up. Maybe I just like my lasagna more saucy. But I felt like this could've used more sauce. Next time I'll use 3 full jars of sauce with 1 jar of water mixed in. You can see in the pictures I shared my lasagna had a lot of layers! I loved it! It was awesome not having to cook the noodles or buy no boil because they tend to be more expensive. I would definitely add some water to your sauce. I covered each layer of noodles with sauce. The uncooked noodles soak up all the liquid they can so the water helps. I also cooked mine at 350 degrees f. I cooked it for an hour covered. Then 1/2 an hour uncovered I don't know how the noodles would've cooked otherwise because for me at 1 hour the noodles were still very undercooked. Sorry for adding all my tweaks I know people don't like it when people tweak recipes. But I believe to always make the recipe work the best way it can for yourself. Thanks for sharing.

Par boiled the pasta. Fresh mushrooms always. Used 1 jar spicy pepper sauce and one basil. Dbl sauce. 22oz each. Added frozen spinach.even with the blanched pasta took at least an hour at 350. Turned up to 375 removed foil and baked for an additional 20 minutes with mozzarella and fresh grated parm

I will make this again. Both my husband and I liked it. I used 1 1/2 jars of spaghetti sauce. Next time I will use 2 jars. I added 1/2 pound of mild Italian style pork to the ground beef. I used 2 containers (8 oz each) of ricotta and omitted the cottage cheese. I added 3 cloves of garlic and some oregano and basil. I used fresh mushrooms. I used my 5 qt Dutch oven to cook it. I ended up with left over noodles and a little left over cheese. Next time, I will be more generous with the cheese layers. No problems with the noodles cooking. Leftovers will go in the freezer. Thanks for the great recipe!

I've been making lasagna without cooking the noodles for more than 30 years. The key to this recipe is that it must be covered tightly with foil. I use 2 pounds of ground beef and LOTS more mozzarella. No cottage cheese or mushrooms in mine. Also, bake at 375º for 1 hour. No need to remove foil, I like my cheese gooey, not hard and crisp. Lasagna is so much easier without cooking the noodles!

I cut this in recipe in half and left out the mushrooms and onions since I don't care for them. I did add a little italian seasoning and salt to the ground beef as I browned it. I had a jar of Ragu in the panty, so I went with that. Easy peasy. I didn't have ricotta, so I added in some shredded mozzarella until the ratio looked good. I added a little water to the jar to get the last bits of sauce out, then poured that on the top of the lasagna. I topped this with shredded mozzarella and parmesan and, since I forgot, I didn't hold back the cheese for the last 15 minutes of bake time. It all went on at the beginning. That's life. It did not affect the final result. I did cook mine another 6 minutes to get the cheesy top browned in a few places because it tastes better with those toasted cheese bits. This was a very good meal and was simple to make. Uncooked noodles are much easier to work with. I only had to break them to fit the loaf pan I made it in. I'd make this again.

I was looking for a simple recipe and this was just that. I took the suggestion to skip the mozzarella between layers and used Romano instead of parmesan there. I also added about 1/2 cup water total poured in the oorners of the pan to make sure the noodles cooked fully. It was a huge hit with my husband who is not crazy about lasagna and my friend who is!

This was my first time not to pre-boil my noodles before making lasagna and after this recipe I will never pre-boil my noodles again. Other people are correct when they say to make the tomato mixture a little watery and sort of thin so the noodles will have enough liquid to cook thoroughly. I did take some suggestions from other posters; I used a lb of ground beef and a 1/2 lb of Italian sausage. I also chopped up fresh garlic and added the garlic to the meat with the onions and added Italian seasoning to the meat mixture also. I also added a little garlic powder to the ricotta/cottage cheese mixture. Next time, I will sprinkle a little salt on the noodles. But this is a no-fail recipe.

This was awesome! I used half ground beef and half italian sausage. I also used gluten-free noodles since I can't have wheat. I boiled the gluten-free noodles until they were almost soft only because they take much longer to cook than regular noodles and I wanted to be sure they were done. It turned out wonderful!

I just took this dish out of the oven. Believe the chef meant to say 1 hr. 45 minutes in the oven at 350 degrees. I tested at 45 minutes, the noodles were uncooked. Tested every 15 minutes until cooked @ 1 hr. 45 minutes. Makes sense as the no cook noodles take a full 55 minutes, with 5 minutes for browning. Needed 3 full jars of sauce for this dish, not 28 ounces as stated. I also had to add 1/4 C of water to the pan to keep the noodles moist. Looks great, though, can't wait to try it.
Use 2 jars of spaghetti sauce and drain the hamburger before adding the onions. Came out great!!!
I used gluten free lasagna noodles. No one noticed and gobbled it up!
This was delicious! I did leave out the cottage cheese because it had no place in Italian food. So bring on the ricotta and make this recipe. It’s fantastic.
It's a humongous recipe. Next time I'll do the 1/2 recipe and leave out the cottage cheese. Seemed like too much of that. Was great to not have to cook the noodles first.
Very easy to put together and tastes great. I added 1/2 lb of pork sausage to the beef. 👌
I used ground chicken and turkey instead of ground beef. It turned out well. I found I needed more mozzarella cheese to cover the top layer.

We really enjoyed this recipe. It was very flavorful and easy to prepare. The only thing that I found was an issue was the noodles did not get fully cooked in the time recommended in the recipe. The noodles were not tender and they weren't al dente either. I followed the directions exactly including covering the pan with foil, and I added additional sauce to increase the liquid content.

I’ve never mixed ricotta and cottage cheese and was pleased with the consistency. The consistency was almost like a roux. I added a 1/8 tsp of nutmeg to the ricotta mixture and the only other change I made was I left out the onion not because I don’t like onion but because I was too lazy to dice an onion the day I made it. But no one misses the onion and I think next time I make this I’ll leave out the onion and double the mushrooms or cook fresh mushrooms instead of canned.

I jokingly refer to this as my "smoked lasagna." I doubled this recipe, omitting only the mushrooms, but one of my pans was only 8.5 x 10". (I needed to give one to my sick sister's family.) My cans of spaghetti sauce were only 24 oz, so I supplemented with an additional jar of sauce, and having read that it was important that all noodles were covered, I wound up using the whole thing. My pans were so full, they both cooked over, filling the kitchen with smoke. Although I have an oven-cleaning chore ahead, and the kitchen still smelled like smoke the next day, fortunately the lasagna did not smell or taste smoky. My husband was very pleased with the lasagna and pronounced it a great success. I thought it was good, but next time I think I'll add some Italian seasoning or fresh herbs. I used garlic and herb plus fresh garden sauce, and I imagine that makes a difference. One warning to senior cooks: these pans are heavy. I had to get my husband's help to move the hot (wet) pans out of the oven. I might divide the ingredients into more, and definitely not quite as full pans. However, the lasagna presents as full, hearty, and generous, which was just what I hoped for. It also held together well when served.
I added Italian sausage to the ground beef and used 2 jars of spaghetti sauce. I also added shredded parmesan cheese to the shredded mozzarella cheese.
